decisions: Secondary is an edge outline with a transparent fill, so it takes the surface it sits on. There is no key-fill token, and the spec says 'edge outline'.

The primary label is body size (1rem) at weight 600, not the lead size (1.25rem) the prototype used. This addresses review finding I5: 'Move the event to Thursday at 3pm and send the message to Priya' wraps to 2 lines at 375 and 3 lines at 320, and keeps its block padding.

Pressed and busy both move the button down by --sv-button-press-depth, using the logical-free translate property. A busy key reads as held down. Both effects animate only when reduced motion is not requested.

Disabled keeps the edge, removes the primary fill and uses text-soft; no opacity is used. Disabled quiet also loses its underline, because the underline is what says it can be pressed. A link (a.sv-button) has no disabled state; the note says to remove the link instead.
Quiet has padding-inline 0, so its text lines up with the column edge. It still has the 48px control height.

The busy mark is ::before with mask var(--sv-icon-busy), background currentColor and forced-color-adjust none. That way it follows the label colour on-solid on the primary, ink on secondary, and stays visible in forced colours. It turns with the keyframe value 1turn. I confirmed the current lint allows that value, but only inside keyframes.

sv-button checks validity without firing events (form.matches(':valid')). It never calls checkValidity, so it does not set off sv-field's invalid handling. It decides on a setTimeout after the submit, so a cancellation by sv-field or sv-error-summary is respected. It reacts only when e.submitter is its own button or absent. While busy it cancels both click and submit, which also covers Enter in a field. It swaps the button's child nodes for data-busy-label and puts them back on pageshow with persisted set.

Checkbox: checked gives an ink tick plus an ink edge. Invalid (:user-invalid or aria-invalid='true') gives a 4px edge in the danger colour, so the state is carried by shape as well as hue. Disabled gives no well, soft text and a soft tick. The row is a flex label with align-items flex-start and space-3 block padding, so the box lines up with the first line of a wrapped label.

Select copies field.css's control values: space-2 by space-3 padding, a thick edge border, radius-control, the well fill, a thin border when disabled, and an error edge of border-inline-start --sv-field-error-edge-width in danger. It sets all of these itself, so it works without field.css. Its specificity (0,1,1) sits under field's [aria-invalid] rule, and that rule does not touch padding, so the chevron keeps its room. In forced colours it returns to appearance auto.

The demo-select markup follows the spec table: div.sv-field holding label, an optional hint, p.sv-field__error (hidden until there is an error) and select.sv-field__control.sv-select. The live example wraps it in <sv-field>, as demo-field and field.js do.
I shortened the demo's delivery option labels after the screenshot showed '£3.95' cut off. A native select cannot wrap. I also added text-overflow: ellipsis.

Note for the lead: each check-screens --only run overwrites gates/raw/2026-11-15-screens.json with that run's screens only. The file now holds only demo-select. A full run is needed before the file is used as a gate.
token_gaps: component.checkbox.error-edge-width: the thicker edge of an invalid checkbox. I used --sv-space-1 (4px), which is a spacing token used as a border width. I would give it 4px, as a border primitive border.width.4.

component.select.mark-stroke (or a semantic stroke width for drawn marks): the stroke width of the gradient chevron. I used --sv-border-thin for a 1px solid core plus about 1px of soft edge on each side, roughly 2.5px in all, to match the icon grid's 2.5 stroke. A 2px stroke token would say this directly.
spec_gaps: Select chevron: the spec asks for the select's own arrow mark, and the task names the chevron mark from src/base/icons.css. That mark is a mask image and can only be coloured through background-color on an element that has it as a mask. A native select has no rendered ::before or ::after. Masking the select itself would also clip its focus outline. Used as background-image, the icon draws in black, which would be invisible in the dark theme. So I drew the chevron as two linear-gradient strokes in currentColor, sized by --sv-select-arrow-size. It follows the theme and goes soft when disabled. Two possible fixes: a part element such as span.sv-select__mark in the spec table, or an icon that can be tinted.

To keep the spec's single-element markup, the gradient chevron's vertex is slightly flat, where the two strokes meet at the edge of their boxes. At 375 dark the chevron is crisp and clearly visible against the well; I zoomed in on it.

Real back-forward cache restore: I tested pageshow with persisted set by dispatching a synthetic PageTransitionEvent, not by a real back navigation.

The teal accent: by the CSS only, --sv-button-primary-fill aliases var(--sv-color-accent), which :root[data-accent='teal'] re-points. I took no screenshot.

decisions: Control is a well: thick (2px) edge border, control radius, inherited body font, min height size-control; textarea is twice the control height and resizes only vertically. The rules suit a select too: they style only the box, and nothing uses :read-only.
Read-only uses [readonly], not :read-only, because :read-only also matches select and disabled controls. It shows a dashed edge with no well fill.

Disabled: thin edge, no well, soft text and soft label (via :has). There is no opacity, because check-screens does not exempt disabled controls from contrast. The demo's hint says why the field is unavailable.
Error edge: border-inline-start is set to the field-error-edge-width token in danger. Hover is excluded on invalid controls so the danger edge survives.
The error line and the summary both have an explicit [hidden]{display:none}, because they set display themselves.

The summary tab is a wide border-inline-start (mark plus 2 x space-3), so it follows the writing direction. The mark is absolutely positioned on it in on-solid. I removed the divider border because the 1px top border made a mitred corner on the tab. The plate is panel-toned, so it belongs on the ground.

The summary listens for submit in the capture phase on the document and marks the event (svChecked). The field's own form handler then skips, so only one handler validates and moves focus. With no summary, the field handler stops an invalid submit, scrolls the label into view and focuses the first invalid control. Without that, novalidate would let bad data through.

Behaviour beyond the spec, for the lead to veto:
- A server-rendered (visible) summary takes focus on load, as in the GOV.UK pattern.
- A shown error clears on input as soon as the value becomes valid; it never appears while the person is typing.
- The summary removes a fixed field's link and hides when none remain.
- sv-field exposes check() and error.
- No validation runs on load, so server-rendered errors stay until the next blur after typing, or the next submit.
When an error clears, the error line is emptied as well as hidden, because a hidden element named in aria-describedby is still read.
Teal: neither component reads --sv-color-accent, so ?accent=teal changes only the borrowed submit button. The danger hue (25) is far from teal (195).
Both demos use the button builder's class="sv-button" data-variant="primary" data-width="full" for the submit button. Its CSS was present in the build when the lint and checks ran.

decisions: Message tab: span.sv-message__mark is absolutely positioned against the plate (inset-block 0). It therefore runs the full plate height whatever the content: one paragraph, a heading and a paragraph, or a paragraph and a quiet button. The plate pads its inline start by the tab width plus space-3. The mark is drawn in on-solid on ::before, aligned to the first line. Text is always --sv-color-text, never soft (fixes I1). On a panel, data-surface="well" switches the plate to --sv-message-surface-on-panel.
No overflow:hidden on the message plate. The tab gets its own start-side radii instead, so a quiet button's focus ring is never clipped.

Status is one span with its words. The tab is ::before (mark-size square, tab radius, tone fill). The mark is ::after, laid over the tab in on-solid, 20px inside the 24px tab. min-block-size is body size x body line height (24px), and vertical-align is top, so it sits in a text line without changing its height. A long label wraps beside the tab, and the tab stays on the first line.

Busy mark: @keyframes rotate(1turn) over --sv-status-busy-duration, linear, only inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. A first version used quarter-turn matrices because the lint then rejected 1turn. The lead has since updated the lint, and I switched to rotate(1turn). The switched version was measured as one clockwise turn per 800ms, with no animation under reduced motion.

Cost-summary rows are flex with wrap. The dt is flex 1 1 0 and keeps min-inline-size auto, so it never shrinks below its longest word: no 'Deliv/ery' (fixes L2). The dd is flex none and nowrap, with margin-inline-start auto, so a wrapped amount stays on the end edge. Unknown rows let the dd wrap at body size with proportional figures.
The cost-summary note p goes inside the total's dd, after the amount. A dl cannot hold a p directly. A second dd in the total row would make the checker measure the 16px note as a total.

The rule above the total is a 1px solid border in --sv-cost-summary-text at full strength, with no opacity. The total label is at the lead size, weight 600, tight line height. The amount is at --sv-cost-summary-total-size, weight 600.
The large-order overflow at 320 is left failing in the checker, not hidden. I did not clip it, scroll it, insert wbr, shrink it, or use a container query.
The quiet button in a message keeps its own padding and is not optically aligned to the text: message.css may not target .sv-button.
Forced colours: the marks switch to CanvasText with forced-color-adjust none. The message plate, cost display and status tab get a CanvasText border, so nothing vanishes.

decisions: I changed the existing small-control fixture (control-too-small.html) without weakening it. Its original markup, a 4 pixel 'i' link inside a sentence, is exactly the case the new rule exempts, so it began to pass (shown in the run before the fixture update). Its link is now display:inline-block, with a comment in the fixture saying why. It still fails control-too-small (4 by 24 pixels), and it now also proves the 'computed display must be inline' condition.
The 1turn exemption covers only the exact token 1turn, and only inside @keyframes. The failing fixtures show that -1turn, 0.5turn and 360deg inside @keyframes, and 1turn outside, still fail css-unit.

System colour names stay in the general named-colour list, so they fail everywhere by default. They are allowed only when every comma-separated branch of the @media query contains (forced-colors: active) and no branch uses 'not'. I chose this strict reading: the bare (forced-colors) form, (forced-colors: none), 'not (forced-colors: active)' and '(forced-colors: active), (min-width: 48rem)' all still fail. Hex values, colour functions and ordinary names such as red still fail inside the block. css-color--system.css shows each of these cases.

A link counts as being in running text only when all of these hold: it is a[href] or [role=link]; it does not have the class sv-button; its computed display is inline; and its parent element has another non-empty text node, or a visible display:inline element with text. A link inside a wrapper element that holds only that link is not exempt, which is the conservative choice. Each exempt control records targetExempt with the text 'inline link in running text (WCAG 2.5.8)' in the JSON, so a pass can be explained.

missing-speaker-label checks only visible .sv-chat-message elements. A label counts only if it is a visible .sv-chat-message__from with non-whitespace text. The existing hidden() function treats a visually hidden label as not visible, so the fixture fails on three cases: no label, a blank label and a visually hidden label.

Proposal height is the rounded height of the tallest visible .sv-proposal. It is stored as results[].proposalHeight and measurements.proposal ({count, height, where}). In the summary table it appears as an extra 'proposal height' row under the screen, shown only when at least one state has a proposal. It is never a finding.

results.summary: I built and measured UI SDK 0.1.0-beta.3 for field, select, checkbox and button, and the recommendation is to stay native for all four. Measured gzip sizes are 22,405, 63,343, 19,212 and 15,628 bytes; together they are 74,857, with 16,714 bytes of shared code. Every bundle is over the 5,120-byte row. With scripts off, both trial pages sent all four fields exactly once; with scripts on, so did both. To get that, select and checkbox needed glue of our own (211 B). Real gains: the select's keyboard popup, and the button's pending state with a one-second announcement. Problems found: a required checkbox outside a field took focus ahead of the first invalid field, and the select probably loses autofill (inferred, not tested). The injected 'ui-sdk' layer sets only display and text-align: no colour, font or size. The 'check' script now runs build before lint.

decisions: Recommendation is to stay native for all four components. Every bundle is 3 to 12 times over the 5,120-byte row, and charter/exceptions.md keeps such a part blocked until the CEO changes the row.

Each component's share in the combined bundle is measured by leaving it out: all four (74,857 B) minus the other three. Results: field 6,869, select 46,988, checkbox 3,106, button 1,180, shared core 16,714. These leave-one-out bundles were built in scratch so they do not add rows to the size table.

Native fallback design: ui-input and ui-button wrap native elements. ui-select and ui-checkbox replace them, so the page carries a native select and checkbox. glue.js copies the person's choice across after upgrade and removes the native control, so each name submits once. The copy-across was verified with a delayed script.
A native <label for> is nested inside ui-field-label, so inputs keep their names with scripts off. ui-field keeps an author-set id, so the native label still works after upgrade.
trial.css is linked before dist/souvenir.css and opens with '@layer ui-sdk, sv.tokens, sv.base, sv.components, trial;' so the injected UI SDK layer has the lowest priority.
The 'check' script order is now tokens, build, lint, size, screens.
spec_gaps: charter/exceptions.md requires native fallback markup for every UI SDK-backed part. For select and checkbox, UI SDK supplies none; its docs point to fallback markup on the component pages, but those pages have none. Meeting the rule takes our own glue script (211 B gzip), which the exception does not mention.

With UI SDK parts mixed on one page, a required ui-checkbox outside a ui-field took focus on an empty submit, ahead of the first invalid field. This breaks the expectation that the first invalid field takes focus.
UI SDK's field error falls back to the browser's English message, which says 'Please'. That breaks charter voice unless a 'match' message is written for every validity case.
not_exercised: Real browser autofill. The select losing autofill is inferred from the markup, not observed.
Screen readers. The announcements were read from DOM live-region text, not heard.
